concerns.text: T101 declares 'Dependency: baseline_test_predictions.csv from completed T014.5 (already present)', but plan T014.5's defined deliverable was baseline_residuals.png — the artifact the verifier rejected. The tasks file simultaneously marks T014.5 complete and re-does its output in T101. If T014.5's deliverables were never materialized, T101's declared input may not exist, making the producer-before-consumer chain unverifiable. Reconcile which baseline artifacts actually exist and, if baseline_test_predictions.csv is missing, add its production to T101 or a predecessor.

T106's inventory asserts 'statistical_test_report.csv' (listed under data/derived/*.csv) and the completed list cites 'statistical_test_report.md', but plan T021.1 produces 'data/derived/statistical_report.md'. The consumer (T106) checks for a filename no producer task ever emits, so the inventory check will fail against the plan-produced file. Pick one canonical name across plan and tasks.

T106 asserts 'data/derived/validation_audit.md' but plan T057 promises 'data/derived/validation_audit.pdf'. Same consumer-expects-unproduced-filename pattern; the T106 dependency on the completed T057 audit cannot resolve unless the format/filename is reconciled.

T105's dependency references 'completed T030.2/T009 artifacts', but no T009 exists in plan.md or elsewhere in tasks.md — a dangling dependency reference. Replace with the actual task ID that produced the needed artifact (likely the preprocessing/data-quality task).

Completed list and T102 read fingerprints from 'data/processed/{full,train,test}_fingerprints.csv' while plan T019.1/data-model specify 'data/processed/*.npy'. Not an ordering violation per se, but the producer/consumer artifact identity drifts between plan and tasks; T102's declared input path should match what the completed fingerprint task actually wrote.
